title: Wright-Patterson AFB Federal Facility Agreement (CERCLA §120)
warnings: Source is an OCR'd scan of the 1991 FFA; the OCR is garbled in places ("PwwLcuu" = Program, "cxarvleted" = completed). Dates, statutory citations, and the Findings of Fact were read against context; verbatim quotes above are normalized only where OCR mangled obvious words.

The administrative docket number is blank on the executed cover sheet in this copy. The document's own metadata keyword is "3/31/91" (the execution/signature date); the FFA becomes formally EFFECTIVE only when U.S. EPA issues its post-public-comment notice (Section 40), a date not stated in this copy — recorded here as execution_date, not effective_date.

fields.agency: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency, Region V (and U.S. Department of the Air Force)
fields.program: CERCLA Section 120 Federal Facility Agreement (Superfund; DoD Installation Restoration Program)
fields.applicant: United States Department of the Air Force (Wright-Patterson AFB)
fields.site_address: Wright-Patterson AFB, Miami River Valley Basin northeast of Dayton, Greene and Montgomery Counties, Ohio — approx. 8,200 acres ("Areas A and C" and "Area B")
fields.affected_resource: Miami Buried Valley Aquifer (the sole-source drinking-water aquifer; 17 WPAFB supply wells + Dayton/Fairborn municipal well fields) contaminated by VOCs (TCE, PCE, carbon tetrachloride, 1,1,1-TCA, chloroform, 1,2-DCE, toluene) from ≥58 base waste-disposal sites.
fields.note: The CERCLA Section 120 Federal Facility Agreement between U.S. EPA Region V and the U.S. Air Force governing Superfund cleanup at WPAFB. Executed 1991 (metadata 3/31/91), following the base's NPL listing on 1989-10-04 (54 Fed. Reg. 41021). Findings of Fact tie the contamination directly to the Miami Buried Valley Aquifer — the SAME sole-source aquifer designated at 53 FR 15876 (see ssa-53fr15876.epa.yaml). This is the [verified] primary instrument behind the WPAFB profile's TCE/PFAS-plume receiving-water dimension.

title: Buried Valley Aquifer System (BVAS), Sole Source Aquifer Petition
warnings: The primary source is a 2006 U.S. EPA Region 5 full-text TRANSCRIPTION of the Federal Register notice ("Not Original Document"), not the original Federal Register page image. All figures below are transcribed verbatim from that transcription.

The petition designated the ENTIRE Buried Valley Aquifer System (BVAS) across nine counties; "Great Miami North" in the source filename is the Ohio-EPA source-water map segment label, not a separate designation. WPAFB (Greene + Montgomery) sits within the designated area.

fields.note: U.S. EPA Region V final determination designating the Buried Valley Aquifer System (BVAS) of the Great Miami/Little Miami River Basins of southwestern Ohio a SOLE SOURCE AQUIFER under SDWA Section 1424(e) (42 U.S.C. 300f, 300h-3(e)), signed by Regional Administrator Valdas V. Adamkus on 1988-04-14, published at 53 Fed. Reg. 15876 (May 4, 1988), FR Doc. 88-9103. Petition submitted by the Miami Valley Regional Planning Commission (complete petition received 1987-11-25); public comment 1987-12-22 through 1988-02-22 drew a single comment, in support. This is the [verified] primary instrument behind the WPAFB profile's sole-source-aquifer claim: the base's drinking-water and plume story rests on this aquifer.

title: Wright-Patterson AFB (88 ABW/CEVO) letter requesting Ohio EPA revoke NPDES permit 1IN00274*AD (Bioslurper unit) — not a permit instrument
warnings: THIS DOCUMENT IS A ONE-PAGE REVOCATION-REQUEST LETTER, NOT A PERMIT. It is Wright-Patterson AFB's 2006-08-09 letter to Ohio EPA asking that NPDES permit 1IN00274*AD be revoked. The corpus holds NO copy of permit 1IN00274 itself — no permit face sheet, no fact sheet, no effluent-limit tables, nothing from Ohio EPA's side of the correspondence. Every field below describes what THIS LETTER SAYS about permit 1IN00274 (its number, its stated expiration date, the reason the base wants it gone) — it is not read off the permit and must not be cited as if it were. Anyone wanting the permit's actual terms (outfall, limits, receiving water, issuance history) has to find that instrument separately; this artifact cannot supply it.

PERMIT 1IN00274 WAS AN INDUSTRIAL PERMIT FOR A BIOSLURPER, NOT A POTW/SEWAGE PERMIT. The letter's second paragraph identifies the regulated unit: "the Bioslurper unit has not be in use for a couple of years" (verbatim, including the document's own grammar — "has not be" rather than "has not been"). A bioslurper is a soil/groundwater vapor-extraction remediation technology, not a wastewater treatment plant. This document is therefore NOT evidence of a municipal sewage-plant permit for Wright-Patterson AFB, and nothing here should be read into a WWTP/POTW context.

WHETHER OHIO EPA ACTUALLY REVOKED THE PERMIT IS [open]. The letter only requests revocation "at the earliest possible date" — it is one half of a correspondence. No response, order, or revocation notice from Ohio EPA is captured in this corpus. Do not write that the permit "was revoked"; the correct statement is that the base asked for revocation on 2006-08-09 and the agency's response is not established by anything held here.

A FEDERAL ENCLAVE HAS NO CITY SEWAGE-PLANT NPDES PERMIT, AND THIS DOCUMENT DOES NOT SUPPLY ONE. Wright-Patterson AFB does not appear in this OEPA batch with a POTW/municipal-sewage permit because it is not a municipality — its land is a federal enclave, not incorporated territory served by a city plant. Do NOT substitute a nearby Dayton-area municipal WWTP permit for WPAFB's own sanitary-sewage disposal, and do not assert that any specific plant treats the base's sewage. Whether and where WPAFB's sanitary flow is treated (on-base package plant, connection to a municipal system, or something else) is `[open]` — no captured source in this corpus answers it. This letter concerns an unrelated industrial remediation permit only.

THE STATED EXPIRATION DATE IS ~20 YEARS IN THE PAST. The letter gives the permit's expiration as 31 December 2006. As of this extraction (2026-08-26), that is roughly twenty years ago. Regardless of whether Ohio EPA ever acted on the revocation request, permit 1IN00274*AD is long expired on its own stated terms.

letter_detail.body_paragraph_1_verbatim: "Per our recent correspondence regarding the National Pollution Discharge Elimination System (NPDES) permit # 1IN00274*AD which is due to expire 31 December 2006, we are requesting that this permit be revoked at the earliest possible date."
letter_detail.body_paragraph_1_note: The document itself prints "National Pollution Discharge Elimination System" — "Pollution" rather than the standard statutory "Pollutant". Verified at 600 DPI; this is the document's own wording, not an artifact of this transcription, and is transcribed verbatim rather than silently corrected to the standard term.
letter_detail.body_paragraph_2_verbatim: "As you've observed on the Form 4500 Monthly Reports, the Bioslurper unit has not be in use for a couple of years. We have no future plans to reuse this piece of equipment and would like to cease further monthly reporting. If you have any questions regarding this issue, please contact Mr. Sherm Siegal, of this office, at (937) 257-8591 or myself at (937) 257-5537."
letter_detail.body_paragraph_2_note: "has not be in use" is printed exactly that way (missing "en") — the document's own grammar, verified at 600 DPI and transcribed as printed rather than corrected to "has not been in use".
letter_detail.stated_reason_for_revocation: The Bioslurper unit has been unused "for a couple of years" as of 2006-08-09, with no future plans to reuse it; the base wants to stop filing the associated Form 4500 monthly reports.
letter_detail.referenced_prior_correspondence: The letter opens "Per our recent correspondence regarding..." — it references an earlier, uncaptured exchange between the base and Ohio EPA about this permit. That prior correspondence is not in this corpus.
letter_detail.referenced_form: Form 4500 Monthly Reports (the recurring compliance filing the base wants to stop submitting)
